shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Both verses carry the exact same plural noun for fools -- כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים (oshb:Prov.13.19) and כְסִילִ֣ים (oshb:Prov.13.20), byte tier -- both inside their own complete antithesis: fulfilled desire is sweet to the soul while fools despise turning from evil (13:19), and one who walks with the wise grows wise while a companion of fools comes to harm (13:20). As with the tongue-noun pairing at Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19, the grouping rests on one repeated content token bridging two independently closed couplets rather than on a continuing construction, so the evidence is thin by the same standard.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping these as separate stand-alone rows was the default and was reconsidered chiefly because of the repeated fools-noun; since that is one shared token rather than a construction run, the cluster call carries the same reduced confidence as the thin catchword pairing at Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19.
